meta.titre: Printer Types: impact versus non-impact, running costs and choosing for a job
meta.sous_theme: Impact and non-impact printers, examples, print technology, cost per page and choice of printer

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A shop owner in Limbe prints three-part sale slips for her customers, while the photo studio next door prints colour pictures of weddings. Both need printers, but not the same kind: one needs a machine that presses through several sheets and the other needs sharp colour. The GCE asks you to define the two groups of printers, to give examples, and to choose and justify a printer for a given job, so the reasons matter as much as the name.

items: A printer is an output device that produces text and pictures on paper.
Ink, toner and ribbons are consumables: they run out and must be replaced.
Resolution is the number of dots in an image; more dots give a sharper picture.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Hard copy and printers

A **hard copy** is output printed on paper; output shown on a screen is a **soft copy**. A **printer** is the output device that produces hard copy. Printers are placed in two groups according to their **print technology**, that is, how the marks are made on the paper.

### Impact printers

An **impact printer** makes marks by a part of the print head physically striking an inked ribbon against the paper. Examples: the **dot-matrix printer** (a head with a column of small pins, 9 or 24, that strike the ribbon and build characters from dots), the line printer and the daisy-wheel printer. They are noisy, slow and give low print quality, but they can print through several layers at once (carbon or multi-part forms), and their ribbons last a long time, so they are cheap to run.

### Non-impact printers

A **non-impact printer** forms the image without striking the paper. Examples:

- **Inkjet**: sprays tiny drops of liquid ink; good colour and photo quality; cartridges are used up quickly and cost a lot per page.
- **Laser**: a laser beam draws the image on a drum, toner powder sticks to it and heat fixes it on the paper; fast, quiet, sharp text; a toner cartridge prints thousands of pages.
- **Thermal**: heats special heat-sensitive paper, used for till receipts; no ink is needed.

| Feature | Impact | Non-impact |
|---|---|---|
| Print technology | Strikes an inked ribbon | No striking: ink drops, toner fixed by heat, or heat on paper |
| Noise | Loud | Quiet |
| Print quality | Low | Higher |
| Speed | Slower | Faster (laser) |
| Carbon or multi-part copies | Possible | Not possible |

### Choosing a printer

Compare print quality, speed, noise, colour, the number of copies needed, the price of the printer, and above all the **cost and rate of consumption of ink, toner or ribbon**.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question gives figures about a printer
variantes.contenu_markdown: Print quality is measured in **dpi** (dots per inch): the higher the dpi, the sharper the print. Speed is measured in **ppm** (pages per minute) for page printers, and in characters per second for many impact printers. Cost per page = price of the cartridge, toner or ribbon / number of pages it prints.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a scenario asks 'which printer would you choose?'
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the printer, then give two reasons taken from the scenario (colour needed, copies needed, volume, budget) and, if the mark scheme allows, one limit of your choice. A choice without reasons earns very little.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question focuses on how the marks are made
variantes.contenu_markdown: Say that an impact printer forms characters by striking an inked ribbon against the paper, whereas a non-impact printer forms them without striking, for example by spraying ink, fixing toner with heat, or heating special paper.

sections.enonce_markdown:
The office of a school in Kumba prints 600 pages of black text every term. It is choosing between two printers. Printer A is an inkjet whose cartridge costs 15 000 FCFA and prints 500 pages. Printer B is a laser printer whose toner costs 45 000 FCFA and prints 3 000 pages. The office also issues three-part carbon receipts.

(a) Calculate the consumable cost per page for each printer.

(b) Calculate the consumable cost of the 600 pages with each printer and say which is cheaper.

(c) Name the type of printer needed for the carbon receipts and give one reason.

etapes.justification: Cost per page = cost of the consumable / pages it prints.
Divide each price by its own page yield.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A: 15 000 / 500 = 30 FCFA per page. B: 45 000 / 3 000 = 15 FCFA per page.

etapes.action: Choose the printer for the receipts.
etapes.justification: Only an impact printer can print through carbon or multi-part paper.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A dot-matrix (impact) printer, because its pins strike the ribbon and press through all the layers.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Printer A: 30 FCFA per page; printer B: 15 FCFA per page. (b) A costs 18 000 FCFA and B costs 9 000 FCFA, so the laser printer is cheaper to run by 9 000 FCFA each term. (c) A dot-matrix printer (impact), because non-impact printers cannot make carbon copies.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that an impact printer is one with a strong impact on the quality of print.
items.pourquoi_faux: 'Impact' describes the way the marks are made: the head physically strikes a ribbon against the paper. It says nothing about quality, which is low.
items.correction_markdown: An impact printer strikes an inked ribbon against the paper.

items.erreur_markdown: Classing the laser printer as an impact printer because a laser 'hits' the paper.
items.pourquoi_faux: The laser only draws the image on a drum; toner is then fixed with heat. Nothing strikes the paper.
items.correction_markdown: Laser, inkjet and thermal printers are non-impact.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that both inkjet and laser printers use toner.
items.pourquoi_faux: Inkjet printers use liquid ink in cartridges, while laser printers use toner powder.
items.correction_markdown: Inkjet: liquid ink. Laser: toner powder.

items.erreur_markdown: Defining a hard copy as a copy of a file kept on the hard disk.
items.pourquoi_faux: A hard copy is output on paper. A copy of a file saved elsewhere is a backup.
items.correction_markdown: Hard copy = printed output on paper; soft copy = output on screen.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that a laser printer can make carbon copies of an invoice.
items.pourquoi_faux: Carbon copies need a striking head that presses through several layers, and only impact printers do that.
items.correction_markdown: Use an impact printer (dot matrix) for multi-part forms.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each printer as impact or non-impact and give one common use: dot matrix, inkjet, laser, thermal.
items.solution_markdown:
Dot matrix: **impact**; multi-part receipts and invoices.

Inkjet: **non-impact**; colour documents and photographs at home or in a small office.

Laser: **non-impact**; fast, sharp black text in offices and schools.

Thermal: **non-impact**; till receipts printed on heat-sensitive paper.

items.enonce_markdown:
A school prints 240 pages of a question paper on a printer rated at 12 ppm. Its cartridge costs 9 000 FCFA and prints 300 pages.

(a) How many minutes does the job take?
(b) What is the consumable cost per page?
(c) What is the consumable cost of the whole job?

A pharmacy must choose between printer X (price 60 000 FCFA, running cost 25 FCFA per page) and printer Y (price 150 000 FCFA, running cost 10 FCFA per page).

(a) Calculate the total cost of each printer after 2 000 pages.
(b) After how many pages are the total costs equal?
(c) Which printer is cheaper for 8 000 pages?
(d) The pharmacy also writes three-part carbon sale slips. Which printer type should it keep for them, and why?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) X: 60 000 + 25 x 2 000 = **110000 FCFA**. Y: 150 000 + 10 x 2 000 = **170000 FCFA**.

(b) 60 000 + 25n = 150 000 + 10n, so 15n = 90 000 and n = **6000 pages**.

(c) At 8 000 pages X costs 60 000 + 200 000 = 260000 FCFA and Y costs 150 000 + 80 000 = 230000 FCFA, so **printer Y** is cheaper.

(d) An **impact (dot-matrix) printer**, because only an impact printer prints through carbon or multi-part paper.

items_markdown: A hard copy is printed output on paper; a printer is the device that produces it.
Impact printers strike an inked ribbon (dot matrix); non-impact printers do not strike (inkjet, laser, thermal).
Only impact printers can make carbon or multi-part copies; non-impact printers are quieter and give better quality.
Inkjet uses liquid ink; laser uses toner powder fixed with heat; thermal uses heat-sensitive paper.
Cost per page = price of the consumable / pages it prints; always use it to compare running costs.
